messages.content: Write the charter for a newly formed platform engineering team. Around 250 words.

# Platform Engineering Team Charter

## Why we exist
Product teams here spend too much of the week on work that isn't product: wiring CI, chasing deploy failures, guessing at Terraform modules. We take that work so they don't have to.

## Mission
Build and run the internal platform (build, deploy, observability, environments) as a product with real users who happen to be our colleagues.

## Scope
We own CI/CD pipelines, deployment tooling, service scaffolding, secrets and config, the observability stack, and cloud infrastructure primitives.

We do not own application code, product roadmaps, or on-call for services we didn't write. We help teams debug their systems; we don't run them for them.

## How we work
- **Paved roads, not gates.** The supported path is the easiest path. Teams can step off it, and then they carry the operational weight themselves.
- **Self-service first.** A request that requires a human ticket is a bug in the platform, and we track it as one.
- **Adoption is the metric.** A tool nobody uses is a failed tool, whatever we shipped.
- **Public roadmap, public incidents.** Trust comes from being predictable, including about our own outages.

## What success looks like in year one
- Empty repo to production service in under a day.
- Deploy frequency up; change failure rate flat or lower.
- Quarterly developer survey: a majority say the platform helps more than it blocks.

## Our commitments to you
Platform questions get answered in a shared channel, not DMs, so the answer outlives the conversation. Breaking changes come with a quarter's notice and a written migration path. If we can't support something well, we say so instead of half-owning it.
Rewrite the text above. Keep the same length and the same purpose. Return only the rewritten text.

# Platform Engineering Team Charter

## Why we exist
Every week, product engineers lose hours to work that has nothing to do with the product: patching CI config, retrying failed deploys, copying a Terraform module and hoping it fits. That work is ours now.

## Mission
Run the internal platform (build, deploy, observability, environments) as a product. Our users are the engineers down the hall.

## Scope
Ours: CI/CD pipelines, deploy tooling, service templates, secrets and config, the observability stack, cloud infrastructure primitives.

Not ours: application code, product roadmaps, on-call for services we didn't write. We will sit with you while you debug your system. We will not become its owner.

## How we work
- **Paved roads, not gates.** The supported path is the cheapest one to take. Step off it if you need to, and the operational weight comes with you.
- **Self-service first.** If a request needs a human to approve a ticket, the platform has a bug. We file it as one.
- **Adoption is the metric.** Shipping a tool nobody adopts counts as a miss, no matter how the demo went.
- **Public roadmap, public incidents.** People trust what they can predict, including our own bad days.

## Year one, done well
- A fresh repo reaches production in under a day.
- Deploys get more frequent while change failure rate holds steady or drops.
- On the quarterly survey, most engineers say the platform helps more than it gets in the way.

## What you can hold us to
Ask platform questions in the shared channel rather than a DM, and we will answer there, so the next person finds the answer without asking again. Breaking changes arrive with a quarter's notice and a written migration path. When we cannot support something properly, we will say so plainly instead of half-owning it and leaving you guessing.
